name: manki-g3-head-slam
notes: Manki ground.3 Head Slam (anim.manki.g3, button 3 in the new numbering), redo to the current GenRA standard, 2026-11-01. The bound clip (manki_ground4_head_slam.anim, session-authored in Codex for PR #271, 2026-10-16) is one of the first GenRA clips. On the v5 'pyro' rig it fails 18 checks: every finger knuckle and middle joint bends backward over ticks 1-33 (up to 110 degrees), both elbows bend backward around the hit, the left wrist folds 128 degrees, the arms snap 69 degrees in one tick at tick 8, the right ankle sinks 6 cm below its idle height during the hit, and it is pose-to-pose (5.8 stops per joint per second, 85% of the joints stopping together, a dead hold over game ticks 10-14 and 35-40). Today's game clock: one 40-tick stage, hitbox on bone.head ticks 10-14 (sphere r 0.5, 14 damage, 28 degrees), IASA 35, a heavy presentation cue at tick 6. The owner allows the frame data to change. This brief authors at 88 ticks, twice a proposed 44-tick game stage: hit from game tick 16 (authored 32) for 5 ticks, IASA game 41 (authored 82), heavy cue at game 12, aim correction ending at game 16 (owner-approved clock, 2026-11-01). Keys stage first; the owner approves the key poses before any motion. Rig pack manki-unity-v5 (2026-10-29) is byte-identical to a fresh snapshot of the live MankiRig.prefab taken 2026-11-01 (rig, idle, fall). 2026-11-01 keys runs: the impact target first asked for the head 0.40 m ahead of the hips, which the 0.393 m hips-to-head chain cannot reach; both takes reached 0.38; lowered to 0.36. 2026-11-01 owner approved take A (the ram) keys and the clock above; keep the deep fold at the impact (t38); plain, short recovery.
character: Manki v5 'pyro' (58 joints: a Humanoid body with Mixamo names, a big head with goggles and a spiky mane, big ears, an open vest and ragged shorts; a two-can spray-can jetpack built into the body mesh and pinned rigidly to Spine2, so it sits on his upper back and turns with the chest; a TORCH-can holster on his left thigh; thumb, index, middle and ring fingers on each hand; arm stretch, forearm offset and fist deform controls that carry the arm skin; a five-joint tail Tail1..5 that a spring drives in the game, so leave it at rest). He is small: hips to head 0.38 m, thigh 0.25 m, shin 0.19 m, upper arm 0.14 m, forearm 0.15 m in this rig. His idle (image 3) is a hunched boxer's crouch: left foot forward, right foot back, knees bent, fists low in front of his hips.
image_notes: 1 and 2: the v5 'pyro' Manki concept the model was built from, front and back. It is a drawing: the rig's proportions rule. 3: the idle on this rig (profile, front, three-quarter rear): the entry and exit pose of this clip.
description:
Manki's ground.3, Head Slam: his heavy grounded normal. He rears back, then drives his big skull forward and down into whoever stands in front of him, like a ram. His head is the hitbox (a big sphere on the head joint), so the head's path is the move: it must arrive well out in front of him, on his centre line, travelling fast during the hit. It sends the victim up and away at 28 degrees, so it should feel like a heavy, solid hit: the whole body throws the skull, not just the neck.

Who he is. Manki is a pyromaniac mad-inventor monkey (images 1 and 2): toothy grin with missing teeth, cracked goggles, a burnt brow, a spray-can jetpack on his back. He is small, wiry and a bit unhinged; his head is huge for his body, and he uses it like a battering ram. Character goes into the wind-up and the hit: the rear-back is a gleeful, exaggerated coil, chin up, grinning at the target. The recovery is plain.

How the game plays it. The match camera sits straight behind him, so the action must read from behind: the head must leave the silhouette of his back and jetpack and appear out in front and below, not stay hidden behind the cans. The game plays this 88-tick clip at about double speed (a 44-tick stage). The fighter does not move or turn in the clip; only the hips joint may translate. The game crossfades in and out over about 0.1 s. Tick 0 and tick 88 are his idle pose exactly (image 3).

Feet. Both feet stay where the idle puts them for the whole clip (left forward, right back): this is a lunge on planted feet, not a step. The left foot and both toes stay planted. The right (back) heel may peel up 2-4 cm while he lunges forward, toes staying on the floor, and comes back down in the recovery. Hold the feet with two_bone leg IK after every body edit and check them with ./genra contacts.

Hands. Fists, clenched the whole clip, as in his idle: the fingers curl toward the palm and the thumb wraps across the closed fingers. Use fist() on both hands. A finger must never bend backward toward the back of the hand (the old clip did, for 33 ticks); the hinge check must pass on every finger at every key. Wrists stay near the line of the forearm (under about 45 degrees); turn the forearm and elbow, not the wrist.

The move (88 ticks, played once; authored at twice the game length):
- Tick 0: idle exactly.
- Tick 10, the lock-on: he settles a little lower (hips down 1-2 cm), the head dips and the chin tucks as he fixes the target; the fists draw in a touch. A small gathering, not a pause.
- Tick 22, rearing back: the weight rolls onto the back (right) foot. The hips shift back 3-5 cm and drop 2-3 cm, the right knee bends more, the front (left) leg straightens. The chest arches back 25-35 degrees from the idle's hunch, the head tips back further with the chin up, grinning at the target. Both arms swing back and up behind him, elbows bent, the fists behind his hips and above them, like a diver about to spring.
- Tick 27, loaded (the hit window is authored 32-40): the hips have already started forward (they lead the strike), while the chest and head are still at their furthest back: the head behind the hips (at least 2 cm behind them, front to back) and high. The arms are at the top of their back-swing. Everything is coiled.
- Tick 33, the strike, mid-drive and fastest: the hips have lunged forward 8-12 cm and down 4-6 cm over the bent front knee, the back leg straightens behind him, the chest pitches forward hard. The head is out in front: at least 0.35 m ahead of the hips, at about the height of his own chest at idle, exactly on his centre line (within 4 cm of the middle, left to right). The arms are swinging forward and down past his sides, fists by his hips, adding to the throw.
- Tick 38, impact and follow-through, late in the hit (window 32-40): the head has driven on, forward and down, to its furthest and lowest: at least 0.36 m ahead of the hips (his spine from hips to head is only 0.39 m, so this is nearly flat) and at least 0.25 m lower than at idle, still on the centre line. The body is compressed behind it: the chest folded forward over the front thigh, the hips at their lowest (6-9 cm down). The arms have kept going a little after the head (overlap): fists forward of the hips, low, elbows bent. This is the squash of the impact.
- Tick 50, rebound: the head comes back up and back as the hips push back over the middle of the stance; the chest rises toward the idle's hunch; the arms come back in toward the body.
- Tick 64, balanced: close to the idle, the weight centred, the back heel down, the fists in front of the hips; only a small difference from idle remains, which settles out by tick 78.
- Tick 88: idle exactly.

Flow. The hips lead every change of direction; the chest trails 1-3 ticks, the head and arms trail more. On the way back the head is the last thing to tip back; on the strike the hips start forward while the head is still back, then the skull whips past them. Keep moving holds, never the same pose twice in a row: the old clip froze for game ticks 10-14 and 35-40. The fists are rigid; the fingers do not flap. The tail is left at rest: the game's spring trails it from the hips. After the hit, the recovery is plain: he regains balance and the arms take the shortest calm path back to his idle. No gesture, no flourish in the ending. The skull keeps travelling through the whole hit window (authored 32-40): no parked head.

fixed: a grounded heavy normal that starts and ends on his idle exactly (ticks 0 and 88)
the head is the hitbox: it must travel fast, forward and down, through the hit window, ending well ahead of him on the centre line
the feet stay planted where the idle has them; the fighter does not move or turn in the clip
adjustable: owner-approved clock 2026-11-01: 88 authored ticks for a 44-tick stage, hit authored 32-40 (game 16-20), IASA authored 82 (game 41); key poses approved (take A)
how far he rears back and how deep the lunge goes, within the beats above
the arm swing's path, as long as it helps throw the head and stays clear of the head and jetpack
